summary: Latency spike (p95/p99) in eu-west after regional failover traffic shift
description:
Customer reports elevated tail latency in eu-west immediately after a regional routing event/failover test window.

Issue summary
- Atlas Payments observed p95 and p99 latency regressions for chat completions in eu-west following a traffic shift into eu-west.
- Time window correlated with the controlled failover exercise (us-east -> eu-west) on 2026-01-15.

Customer impact (as reported)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming + non-streaming)
- Symptoms: p99 increased from ~1.2–1.8s baseline to 4–8s; intermittent timeouts on a subset of requests.
- Business impact: degraded interactive UX; retries increased; no data loss reported.

Environment
- Prod, eu-west
- Customer tier: enterprise
- Models: redwood-llama-3-70b-instruct (primary), redwood-embed-v3 (minor; used in same workflow)

Initial triage notes (Support)
- Confirmed event correlation with internal game day timeline.
- No broad eu-west region outage detected; errors were limited, but tail latency panels showed elevated queueing.
- Asked customer for:
  - request IDs (x-redwood-request-id)
  - timestamps in UTC
  - whether they pinned model version and whether fallback was enabled

Internal investigation summary
- Routing: During the controlled failover window, additional traffic was steered into eu-west as part of the exercise.
- Capacity/headroom: eu-west GPU pool headroom dropped below the effective safe threshold for this model/tenant mix; autoscaler lag + warm-up contributed to transient queue buildup.
- Threshold behavior: Capacity signal was present but did not gate the traffic shift aggressively enough (threshold too permissive for the observed load shape and concurrency spikes). This allowed queue depth to grow, impacting p95/p99.
- Secondary contributors:
  - API gateway retry budget amplified concurrent load during slow responses (clients retried quickly; retry-after not consistently triggered for this path in eu-west).
  - Some requests carried long prompts (high input tokens) that increased per-request service time; with reduced headroom this disproportionately affected tail.

What we checked
- eu-west dashboards (latency + saturation): p99 latency, inflight/queue depth, GPU utilization, batch sizes.
- Region health signals: no reachability failure; error burn within bounds, but latency burn spiked.
- Request traces: sample traces showed increased time in queue/wait-for-worker vs model execution time.
- Dedicated pool: no hardware faults; primary symptom was saturation/queueing.

Mitigation taken (during/after window)
- Allocated temporary burst capacity in eu-west for the impacted pool and increased min replicas for the model serving group.
- Adjusted routing weights to reduce eu-west share for this tenant while headroom recovered.
- Enabled/tuned overload behavior to return clearer backpressure (retry-after) instead of long-tail hanging for a subset of calls.

Current status
- As of 2026-01-16 02:30 UTC, p95/p99 returned to baseline and queue depth normalized.

Customer-facing note (to send/confirm)
- This was a transient tail latency regression associated with a planned resiliency exercise that shifted traffic. We did not observe data integrity issues. We’ve increased eu-west headroom and are tightening capacity gating for future automated/controlled traffic shifts.

Follow-ups / action items
- Tune capacity headroom thresholds and gating logic for failover traffic shifts (Routing + Fleet/Capacity). Linked: ENG-2414.
- Confirm api-gateway retry/timeout behavior and ensure retry-after applies consistently for overload during regional events. Linked: ENG-2419.
- Add explicit annotations to dashboards for automated weight changes to speed future triage. Linked: INT-1149.
- Incorporate this scenario into the next game day success criteria: tail latency must remain within agreed bounds or the controller should halt/rollback the shift. Linked: ENG-2426.

Requested from customer
- 3–5 sample request IDs + timestamps for confirmation in traces (optional now that we’ve correlated internally, but helpful for closing the loop).

resolution: Resolved by increasing eu-west serving headroom (burst capacity + higher min replicas) and reducing routing weight while autoscaling caught up. Root cause was transient saturation/queueing after a planned traffic shift; capacity headroom thresholds for gating were too permissive for the observed load shape. Follow-up work filed to tighten routing capacity thresholds and ensure overload/retry-after behavior is consistent during regional events.
